A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OrdShap work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original attribution experiments on EICU, MIMICIII, IMDB, and synthetic data, together with a medical case study and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a sampling-sensitivity experiment in Appendix E.3.

M1.justification: The OrdShap definitions, value and position summaries, and sampling and least-squares algorithms retain the same procedures. The grouped-position extension already appears in v1 Appendix B.1; v2 expands its explanation.

E1.justification: Both evaluate EICU and MIMICIII mortality and length-of-stay tasks, IMDB sentiment, and the same synthetic problems. The added sensitivity analysis uses existing EHR tasks without introducing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding attribution comparisons retain DeepLIFT, Integrated Gradients, KernelSHAP, LIME, LOCO, and Random. The relocated runtime comparison also retains its original comparator membership.

E3.justification: The new Appendix E.3 experiment uses 100 explanation samples and nine combinations of subset count K and permutation count L, each taking values 10, 50, and 100. Existing benchmark splits, models, metrics, and 200-sample evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused sensitivity analysis examining how K and L affect standard errors of the OrdShap-PI position-importance metric on four EHR tasks. The synthetic analyses and medical case study are retained; runtime evaluation is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors for attribution metrics and standard deviations for runtimes. v2 integrates existing appendix standard errors into Table 2 and uses the same reporting practice for its sensitivity results; no new seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is specified.

E6.justification: v2 Table 7 adds sensitivity results, including EICU-LOS standard errors of 0.0046 across all nine configurations. Existing benchmark scores, uncertainties, and runtimes match after transposition, relocation, and equivalent rounding. Section 4.3 also corrects the negative positional coefficient attribution from 'Hat' to 'Bag,' consistent with the unchanged Figure 3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 1–2, Corollary 2.1, and Appendix C proofs retain their substance. The null-player axiom receives a notation correction from v to omega, without changing its mathematical meaning.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same claims: disentangling value and position importance, connecting OrdShap to Sanchez-Bergantiños values, providing two approximation algorithms, and demonstrating the approach empirically.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly acknowledges that OrdShap-PI requires a separate positional axiomatization, which remains future work, whereas the established connection concerns OrdShap-VI. v1 discusses computational limitations without this explicit qualification.

D1.justification: The new checklist states that source code will be provided for review and that public release depends on internal review; it does not establish an actual public release. v2 also omits v1's detailed optional sparsity-based acceleration suggestion, while retaining the principal implementation and preprocessing details.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kumar et al. on problems with Shapley-based explanations and Theissler et al.'s time-series explainability review. Section 2 modestly refines the independence discussion and comparison with PoSHAP, while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds EHR background in Appendix A.2, localized explanatory edits, acknowledgements, and a NeurIPS checklist. Runtime discussion moves into Section 6.4, but the main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 is transposed and incorporates standard errors previously separated into an appendix table. The runtime table moves from v1 Appendix Table 7 to v2 main-text Table 3, and a new sensitivity Table 7 appears. Existing figures are retained with placement and caption adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and transparency through the explicit OrdShap-PI axiomatization limitation, correction of the toy-example explanation, and integration of existing uncertainty and runtime information into the main presentation. The added sensitivity analysis provides limited supporting evidence, although its standard errors do not establish approximation accuracy. These are modest gains without a substantive change to the method or main benchmark evidence.
